title: Among the Roots
logline: Every turning in the mangrove channels looks the same to a stranger, but a lagoon fisher who grew up in them reads the roots like streets, and spends the low tides planting more.

object.note: Object 4 (identity not chosen) may appear subtly, for example among Chathura's things while he travels, waits or watches, only where it sits naturally in a real moment. Never staged, never the subject.

thread_in.thread: After the rush breaks into sudden quiet, a different kind of lostness: mangrove channels where every turning looks the same, and a fisher who reads the roots like streets.

thread_out.thread: Roots that hold a shore in place become a rope that holds an animal to its circle: what keeps us going round, even when the rope is long.

lesson.in_simple_terms: What keeps us stuck is not always what started it. The texts call greed, hatred and confusion 'roots' because they hold the mind in place the way roots hold a tree up, and they name good roots too: letting go, goodwill and understanding.
lesson.in_simple_terms_si: ගසක් නොවැටී සිටින්නේ මුල් නිසා සේම, සිත යම් දෙයක තදින් එල්ලී සිටින්නේද මුල් වැනි ගති නිසාය; ඒ අතර ආශාව, තරහ, මුළාව මෙන්ම අත්හැරීම, හිතවත්කම, නුවණ වැනි හොඳ මුල්ද තිබේ.
lesson.the_teaching: The Abhidhamma names six roots (hetu): greed, hatred and delusion, and their opposites, non-greed, non-hatred and non-delusion. Both texts say plainly that these are not called roots because they make a mind arise; they are roots because they hold the mind firmly on its object, as a tree's roots keep it standing. In the texts' tables, delusion is present in every unwholesome mind, and Pradeepika adds that the wholesome roots are the stronger: non-greed can overcome greed, non-hatred hatred, and understanding delusion.
lesson.how_the_film_shows_it: At first the boat noses through channels that all look alike, and the viewer is as lost as any stranger. Slowly the fisher's small landmarks, a bent root, a gap in the canopy, teach the eye to see differences, while mature prop roots hold against a running tide. At low tide the seedlings pushed into the mud, and later checked to see which took hold, let the viewer sense that what grows and holds can be tended.

key_terms.en: root; what holds the mind firmly on its object

lesson.caution: This is not 'root cause analysis': the texts explicitly deny that these roots cause a mind to arise, and the stronger good roots are not a general promise that positivity wins.
lesson.builds_on: The market showed attention shaken loose; this film asks what, beneath the shaking, keeps the mind gripped, and finds that confusion runs under every harmful state.
lesson.evidence_class: editorial interpretation grounded in cited source teaching
